claims.value: WT1..WT5, K1..K5 (light); "SILAC heavy spike-in standard (immortalized WT MEF) in <exp>" (heavy)
claims.evidence: MaxQuant experimentalDesignTemplate.txt assigns the 50 raw files to 10 Experiments WT1-WT5 and K1-K5 (5 SCX fractions each); file names carry the same tokens. Light source names = these MaxQuant experiment names. One heavy source per mixture because the same standard lysate is spiked into every sample and build forbids reusing one source at the same fraction/replicate across runs (precedent PXD002669/PXD009766).

claims.location: assay name, comment[data file], comment[fraction identifier] rows 1-100
claims.evidence: All 50 .raw files in the PRIDE list are claimed; each mixture is 5 files SCX1..SCX5 and MaxQuant Fraction column = 1..5 for SCX1..SCX5. Each file appears once as light and once as heavy. combined_SILAC.zip is search output, not a run.
Each mixture was injected once per SCX fraction (one raw file per experiment and fraction in the PRIDE list and MaxQuant design); no repeated injections.

claims.value: SILAC light = individual MEF sample (WT1-5, K1-5)
claims.evidence: PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol: "Each unlabeled lysate was mixed at a 1:1 protein ratio with 25µg of total cell lysate of the SILAC labeled cells." summary.txt: Multiplicity 2, Labels0 empty (light, unlabelled), Labels1 "Arg10;Lys8" for all 50 files. Global median normalized H/L 0.97-1.13 per experiment (1:1 mix) -> both channels present in every run.

claims.value: SILAC heavy = spike-in standard; sample type reference
claims.evidence: PRIDE protocol: "Spike-in SILAC standard was produced by culturing immortalized WT MEF in SILAC DMEM ... supplemented with heavy ... 13C615N2-L-lysine (lysine 8) and heavy 13C615N4-L-arginine (arginine 10) for 9 passages." summary.txt Labels1 = Arg10;Lys8. Data check: log2 Intensity H correlates more tightly across the 10 experiments (median pairwise Pearson 0.942, min 0.900) than log2 Intensity L (0.933, min 0.885), consistent with one common heavy standard. The heavy channel is a quantification reference, not a study group (super-SILAC-style spike-in design, precedent PXD009766).
Light channel holds the individual WT or mutant MEF lysates that are compared.
MaxQuant experiments and file names WT1-WT5; abstract/PRIDE description compares MEFs from Eif2b5R132H/R132H mice with wild-type MEFs.

PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol: "K2, K3, K4, K5 are referred to as Mut1, Mut2, Mut3 and Mut4 respectively" (K = mutant); PRIDE description/abstract: "mouse embryo fibroblasts (MEFs) isolated from Eif2b5R132H/R132H mice". K1 is the fifth mutant culture, omitted from the paper analysis for low identifications (same note). Genotype not independently verifiable from the data: the R132H site (SLGDVLR|DVDAK, Eif2b5 Q8CHW4 aa 126-137) was identified only in the heavy state by ISO-MSMS; light partner intensities are interference (H/L ~0.05 vs global ~1.05) in WT and K alike (r132_evidence.txt).
PRIDE protocol: standard = "immortalized WT MEF".
The heavy channel is a common reference spiked into every sample, not a compared group (precedent PXD009766 heavy reference rows factor value not applicable).

Numbers restart per genotype group and give one number per independently processed MEF sample (README.adoc:330; campaign rule 3). Each WTn/Kn is a separately seeded and lysed MEF culture (PRIDE protocol: "4.3*10^5 MEFs were seeded on 10cm plate ... Cell pellets were lysed"); whether each derives from a different embryo is not stated (see limitations).
One standard culture/lysate (immortalized WT MEF, Lys8/Arg10) spiked into all mixtures -> the same number in every heavy row.
PRIDE organisms NEWT:10090 Mus musculus; MaxQuant FASTA "UniprotKB Nov2014\MOUSE.fasta" (parameters.txt); NCBITaxon:10090 in OLS.

Samples are mouse embryonic fibroblasts (abstract: "mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) isolated from Eif2b5R132H/R132H mice"; standard = immortalized WT MEF). UBERON:0000922 embryo. PRIDE organismParts also lists "brain" (BTO:0000142): that refers to primary astrocytes used only in non-MS assays (abstract: mass spectrometry of total proteome of MEFs; astrocyte work = respiration/mtDNA/glycolysis); no raw file name or MaxQuant experiment is astrocyte.
MEFs = mouse embryonic fibroblasts (abstract); CL:2000042 embryonic fibroblast (OLS).
Cells were isolated from embryos (MEF); exact embryonic day not available. EFO:0007725 embryo stage (OLS).
Wild-type MEFs and the WT standard; PATO:0000461 normal.

Eif2b5R132H/R132H mice are the VWM disease model studied (abstract: mutations in eIF2B subunits lead to VWM; MEFs from Eif2b5R132H/R132H mice). MONDO:0800448 (general VWM term; gene-specific MONDO subtypes not used because the mouse mutation is a model, not a human subtype).
MEFs isolated from mice and cultured; not described as immortalized or as a named line.
PRIDE protocol: "immortalized WT MEF".

PRIDE: "data dependent mode using a top 10 method"; raw: TopN 10, FULL MS / DD-MS2.

Raw method dd-MS2 resolution 17,500 (Orbitrap); MaxQuant searched spectra as HCD FTMS.

Mouse background and embryo sex are not given in the PRIDE record or abstract; full text inaccessible.

limitations: Full text of the paper (J Neurochem 2017, doi:10.1111/jnc.14024) could not be read: not in PMC/Europe PMC full text, Unpaywall/Wiley pdfdirect HTTP 403 (not bypassed). Sample-level facts come from the PRIDE record, MaxQuant outputs and raw headers; strain, sex, embryonic day, passage and culture medium of the light MEFs are therefore not available.

Whether WT1-WT5 and K1-K5 are MEFs from five different embryos per genotype (biological replicates) or repeated cultures is not stated in accessible evidence; each is a separately seeded/lysed culture and is numbered 1-5 within its genotype.

Samples WT5 and K1 are annotated (deposited and in the MaxQuant search) although the PRIDE note says they were omitted from the published analysis for low identifications; K2-K5 correspond to the paper's Mut1-Mut4.

Genotype per sample cannot be confirmed from the data: Eif2b5 R132H removes the R132 tryptic site, but SLGDVLR was identified only in the heavy (WT standard) state; light intensities for it are interference, equal in WT and K samples. Genotype rests on the sample names (WT / K=Mut) given by the submitter.
characteristics[disease] for mutant MEFs = VWM disease model genotype; the abstract notes fibroblasts are not involved in the disease. Annotation choice, not a clinical diagnosis.

The heavy-channel orientation check is weak by design (both channels are MEF): it relies on the explicit protocol statement, MaxQuant Labels1=Arg10;Lys8 and a slightly tighter cross-experiment correlation of H intensities.
PRIDE organismParts lists brain (astrocytes); no deposited MS run is from astrocytes, so brain is not annotated.
